# bash_legacy_notallow.txt — commands that must NOT be allowed with the
# fixture list in legacy_patterns.txt loaded. Expected verdict: anything
# but Allow (normally Continue, i.e. the human is asked; a tier-1 Deny
# also passes). No LLM, no cache.
#
# Every line starts with a listed prefix and then carries something no
# pattern approved. `true` and `echo` stand in for an unlisted command.

# --- compound separators after a listed call ---
acme-cli status; true
acme-cli status;true
acme-cli status && true
acme-cli status || true
acme-cli status & true
acme-cli status &

# --- pipe into an unlisted command, a shell or an exec wrapper ---
acme-cli logs | echo
acme-cli logs | sh
acme-cli logs | bash
acme-cli logs | /bin/sh
acme-cli logs | xargs echo
acme-cli logs | head | true

# --- escaped or quoted command word ---
\acme-cli status
"acme-cli" status
acme-cli status; \true
acme-cli status && \echo hi
acme-cli logs | \true

# --- substitutions carry code the pattern never saw ---
acme-cli status $(true)
acme-cli status `true`
acme-cli status <(true)
acme-cli status "$(true)"
acme-cli status ${X:-$(true)}
acme-cli status $((1+1))
acme-cli status ${!X}
acme-cli status ${X[$Y]}

# --- here-strings and file redirects ---
acme-cli status <<< 'true'
acme-cli status < input.txt
acme-cli status > output.txt
acme-cli status >> output.txt
acme-cli status >&output.txt

# --- env assignment, grouping, control flow ---
X=1 acme-cli status
(acme-cli status)
{ acme-cli status; }
! acme-cli status
for i in 1 2; do acme-cli status; done
if acme-cli status; then true; fi

# --- not on the list at all ---
acme-cli restart
true
